expected_result:
Print Quality Tips and Tricks

(Image)

Many factors can influence your print quality. For great
prints, check our list of tips and see what you like
best.


(Use the colored Print Quality Card)
(Update the firmware)
(Edit Photos)
(Use HP Paper)
(Cool Down)

Use the colored Print Quality Card

Each roll of HP Sprocket Panorama paper has a special blue card.
This is the HP Print Quality Card. Always load the card from the 
same roll of photo paper as is currently in the printer. This card
cleans, calibrates, and prepares your printer for that specific roll
of paper! Keep the colored sheet close by when printing. 

Think you see some print issues? Load the colored sheet again in
the printer to fine tune the print quality for that roll of paper.
When you open a new roll of paper, repeat the process every
time! As a reminder, load the colored card into the paper slot with
the barcode facing down.

steps:
1. Go to account How to & Help
2. Go to Print Quality Tips and Tricks
test_data: Help Page (Print Quality Tips and Tricks) (Continued)
expected_result:
Update Firmware

Keep your printer firmware up to date. Make sure your printer is
charged at least 25% to update your firmware. You will be
automatically prompted when firmware updates are available.
The update will take a few minutes. During this time, stay in the
Sprocket Panorama app and if possible, connect your phone to a
power source during the update to prevent interruptions.

Edit Photos

Use the Sprocket app editing features to adjust color, brightness, contrast, and other factors in your prints, such as adding text and drawings.

Use HP Paper

We reccomend using HP branded paper for the best results. You can
purchase genuine HP Sprocket Photo Paper at (Hyperlink  https://sprocketprinters.com/collections/paper-and-cartridges). Store your
photo paper roll in a cool, dry place and avoid contact with water.

Cool Down

Allow a few minutes for your printer to cool down between
prints. Sprocket priners use heat to activate hidden ink in
your photo paper-with prints sent back-to-back, your printer
works overtime to keep cool! If you get an app message warning
about the printer temperature don't worry too much-the
printer will slow its print speed or pause automatically if it begins
to get warm. You can also try giving your printer a break between
print sessions if it's continually showing as too warm.

(Back to top arrow button)
